chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

It was in the bequest of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to the Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God and His peace be upon him): 'And as for charity, give to your utmost, give to your utmost, until it is said, "He has been extravagant," though you will not have been extravagant.'

key_terms.أَسْرَفْتَ: You have been extravagant/profligate — from إسراف, excess in spending
key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: Voluntary charity (sadaqa), broader than obligatory zakat, encompassing all charitable giving
key_terms.جُهْدَكَ: Your utmost effort/capacity — from جَهْد, implying maximum exertion until one's limits are reached
key_terms.وَصِيَّةُ: Bequest, final instructions or testament — here the Prophet's spiritual and ethical instructions to Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet bequeath to Imam Ali about charity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a portion of the Prophet's (SAWW) bequest to Imam Ali (AS) regarding charity, instructing him to give so generously that others might think it excessive — while in reality it is not. This teaching was addressed to the Imam of the believers himself, underscoring that true Islamic charity should push the boundaries of generosity without crossing into genuine waste. The repetition of 'give to your utmost' (جُهْدَكَ جُهْدَكَ) is an emphatic rhetorical device indicating the highest degree of exertion.
